score_rationale.quantification: IEX numbers don't reconcile: 686.7 ns/event implies ~1.46M/s, not 1.26M/s; a 120 ns p50 with 1.2 µs p99 sits oddly beside a 687 ns mean.
score_rationale.credibility: The order-book work reads as genuine, but an HFT interviewer will check the latency numbers against each other. Right now they disagree, which is the fastest way to lose trust.

must_fix: clarify: 1.26M events/sec and 686.7 ns/event don't match (1/686.7 ns ≈ 1.46M/s). State what each one measures (e.g. parse+match vs match only, or wall-clock vs per-event timer) or make them agree.

clarify: p50 120 ns / p99 1.2 µs (2M-event run) vs 686.7 ns mean (full run, 1.40 GHz). If they come from different runs, clock settings or scopes, say so. Otherwise the mean is far above p50 but below p99 in a way that needs a heavy p99.9 tail to explain.
